meta.scope: Architecture-level engineering tradeoffs for the six-theme risk view
meta.disclaimer: These descriptions interpret physical mechanisms and the reviewed evidence. They are not company scores, rankings, calibrated success probabilities, or claims that an entire approach has passed a requirement. Fuel and plant choices can change an individual project's exposure.
meta.rendering_rule: Render the six descriptions as qualitative text. Do not convert their wording or source count into a numerical or color-ranked risk score.
meta.source_rule: All source IDs resolve in the canonical sources array.
meta.normalization_note: Fifteen normalized approaches: eleven base mechanisms plus levitated_dipole, electrostatic, hybrid_direct_drive and hybrid_fast_ignition. EX-Fusion maps to laser_direct with fast_ignition as a variant.

profiles.scope_note: Conventional tokamaks, especially proposed D-T thermal plants; design-specific current-drive and pulsing choices still matter.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Substantial D-T experimental heritage supports this route. Reactor operating points still require control of transport, instabilities and disruptions together.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Heating, current drive and plant auxiliaries consume electricity. Plasma Q alone cannot establish net output after those loads and thermal conversion.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Long pulses support control and exhaust development. Sustained reactor conditions, current maintenance and recovery between pulses remain distinct demonstrations.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: A D-T plant needs startup tritium, adequate breeding, rapid extraction and recycling. Blanket coverage must coexist with ports and other systems.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Neutrons challenge structural life and shielding; concentrated exhaust challenges divertors. Replacement access and downtime belong in the plant assessment.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Experimental maturity reduces some physics uncertainty. Large integrated systems, qualified manufacturing and component replacement still determine cost and availability.

profiles.scope_note: Low-aspect-ratio tokamak variant; compactness is a geometry choice rather than evidence of cheap electricity.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: High-pressure compact plasmas are attractive, but a high-temperature result does not establish reactor gain, stability or an integrated D-T operating regime.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Current drive, magnet operation and cooling must fit the compact configuration. A smaller core does not by itself reduce recirculating power per net megawatt.

sustained_operation.interpretation: The geometry retains tokamak current and exhaust questions. Long-duration operation must be demonstrated with the intended center-column and heating design.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: For D-T designs, limited inboard space makes allocation among magnets, shielding and breeding material consequential; a complete breeding balance remains necessary.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: The compact center column needs protection and a credible replacement strategy. Exhaust and neutron exposure remain reactor-scale component requirements.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Reduced dimensions could help some construction costs, while constrained access or frequent center-column replacement could offset that benefit; compare complete plant cases.

profiles.scope_note: Externally shaped three-dimensional confinement; coil architecture varies, including nonplanar coils and planar-coil arrays.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Optimized fields reduce reliance on a large tokamak-like plasma current. Long-pulse stellarator results do not yet establish D-T reactor performance.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Reduced current-drive demand is a potential benefit. Plasma heating, cryogenics, pumps and conversion losses must still appear in the complete electrical ledger.

sustained_operation.interpretation: The magnetic configuration suits sustained operation; fuel control, exhaust, component life and maintenance still govern the plant's actual duty and availability.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: D-T breeding and processing requirements remain. A three-dimensional vessel must provide sufficient blanket coverage while leaving access for services and maintenance.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Field accuracy and component access matter alongside neutron and heat exposure. Planar-coil alternatives change the manufacturing problem without eliminating reactor protection requirements.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Optimization and new magnet methods may simplify construction. Modeled availability or component lifetimes are design assumptions until validated in relevant operation.

profiles.scope_note: Linear mirror systems; current D-T commercial examples still need a thermal path for neutron energy.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Open ends make particle and energy losses central. Strong end magnets support confinement development but do not alone establish sufficient fusion gain.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Recovering escaping charged-particle energy may reduce consumption. Recovery of externally supplied heating is different from new fusion electricity or net plant output.

sustained_operation.interpretation: A linear steady-operating design must sustain adequate confinement while continuously handling end losses, fueling and exhaust at the intended conditions.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: D-T versions require breeding and processing despite their open geometry. Alternative fuel plans need their own supply and reaction-performance evidence.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: End exhaust, collection hardware and magnet shielding need relevant lifetime data. Direct access is a possible maintenance advantage, not a measured plant availability.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Linear construction may simplify assembly. The economic case still depends on confinement, heating efficiency, energy recovery and full-system component life.

profiles.scope_note: Beam-sustained FRCs as represented by TAE; its p-B11 goal is a company fuel choice, not a property of every FRC.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Beam formation and sustainment are demonstrated research directions. Extending performance to the intended advanced fuel adds temperature, confinement and radiation-loss requirements.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Neutral beams supply substantial energy; their electrical efficiency and the plasma's loss channels must be included before inferring useful plant gain.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Sustaining an experimental FRC does not establish long-duration reactor operation. Beams, end regions, fueling and control must remain compatible over the required duty.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: A p-B11 plant avoids relying on a primary D-T breeding cycle, but still needs specified fuel purity, preparation, recovery and byproduct management.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Predominantly charged primary products could reduce neutron burdens. Side reactions, radiation, heat loads and beam hardware still require protection and lifetime evidence.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: A linear, high-pressure core may simplify parts of the plant. That potential depends on efficient beam systems and validating the intended fuel regime.

profiles.scope_note: Pulsed magnetic compression and inductive recovery as represented by Helion; current experimental fuels and intended D-He3 cycle remain separate fields.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Formation, merging and compression must produce adequate fusion output in the intended fuel regime; individual temperature or pulse results address only part of this requirement.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Inductive return includes recovered pulse energy. Measure the fusion contribution and all losses over a complete cycle with equal starting and ending stored energy.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Repetitive operation couples pulse timing to coil fatigue, switches, heat removal and recovery. Single-pulse success does not validate power-plant repetition or availability.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: The intended D-He3 cycle needs a credible helium-3 production and recycling balance. D-D reactions and their tritium byproducts must remain in that accounting.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Charged-product conversion could change shielding demands, but D-D side-reaction neutrons and repeated electromagnetic and thermal stresses still affect hardware life.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Direct conversion could simplify the electricity path. Fuel production, durable pulsed hardware and demonstrated integrated net output remain prerequisites for the cost claim.

profiles.scope_note: Sheared-flow-stabilized plasma Z-pinch; do not conflate fusion-plasma experiments with repetitive nonfusion engineering platforms.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Flow shear is intended to suppress pinch instability. Relevant ion conditions, duration and gain must accompany pressure measurements and high-current scaling.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Avoiding external confinement magnets removes one subsystem, not the electrical ledger. Pulse delivery, plasma coupling, fusion gain and conversion all remain consequential.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Frequent pulses require durable electrodes, reliable liquid-metal handling and complete reset. A repetitive hydrogen engineering test does not establish repetitive fusion gain.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: A D-T version still needs tritium supply, breeding and recovery. A proposed liquid-metal system must demonstrate its fuel-processing role as well as cooling.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Electrodes and current-carrying components face local wear; the chamber faces heat and neutron exposure. Renewable liquid protection remains an integrated engineering requirement.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: A compact core and simpler magnet inventory could reduce some costs. Pulse hardware, consumables, cooling and replacement frequency determine whether those savings survive integration.

profiles.scope_note: Mechanically compressed magnetized plasma, especially General Fusion; distinguish experimental solid liners from future renewable liquid walls.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Compression must preserve fuel quality and confinement while raising reaction rates. Electron temperature, inferred ion temperature and D-T-equivalent modeling are different evidence.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Mechanical or electromagnetic compression consumes energy. Useful gain requires the complete compression, thermal conversion and auxiliary balance, not temperature alone.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Each compression must leave a recoverable chamber and a fresh plasma target. Repeatable liner or liquid-wall behavior is distinct from one successful compression.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: Lithium-containing walls may combine breeding and heat capture. Tritium extraction and replenishment must work under the actual pulsed fluid and temperature conditions.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: A renewable liquid wall could protect permanent structures. Mixing, erosion, corrosion, moving components and access can shift rather than eliminate maintenance burdens.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: The concept trades some confinement demands for compression and fluid engineering. Commercial cost depends on reliable repeated operation and integrated, demonstrated gain.

profiles.scope_note: Laser indirect drive through a hohlraum; NIF is predecessor physics evidence, not any startup's own demonstrated plant.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: NIF establishes ignition and target gain above one for this family. Larger or more manufacturable commercial targets still require their own validated performance.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Laser wall-plug efficiency, energy transfer through the hohlraum, target gain and thermal conversion multiply together; target breakeven alone leaves substantial plant demand.

sustained_operation.interpretation: A power plant needs repeated high-gain shots, target delivery and chamber recovery. Cryogenic-layer production or one successful shot does not establish that integrated rate.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: D-T must be manufactured into targets, tracked through the factory and chamber, replenished by breeding and recovered from unburned fuel and debris.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Optics, chamber surfaces and blankets face neutrons, radiation and target debris. Protection, clearing and replacement must support the intended operating schedule.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Laser infrastructure and consumable targets both enter cost. Target price per shot becomes meaningful only with net output, repetition and replacement assumptions attached.

profiles.scope_note: Direct-drive laser family; show hybrid-direct-drive and fast-ignition variants explicitly rather than assuming one common pulse sequence.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Illumination symmetry and laser-plasma coupling are central. Fast-ignition variants add separate energy-deposition requirements; indirect-drive ignition does not validate each variant's gain.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Direct coupling may avoid some indirect-drive losses. Driver efficiency, target gain, any separate ignition driver and plant conversion still determine net output.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Targets and multiple beams must align repeatedly at relevant energy. High-rate irradiation of surrogate targets is component evidence, not high-rate fusion ignition.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: D-T variants require breeding and target-factory inventories. An advanced-fuel variant needs a separate reaction and fuel-processing assessment; laser drive does not determine fuel.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Final optics and chamber structures need protection from repeated bursts and debris. Target and shielding design can change exposure without proving component lifetime.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Potential coupling gains compete with laser, target and alignment requirements. Simulation-derived gain and manufacturing claims require separate validation before projecting electricity cost.

profiles.scope_note: Electrical-pulse-driven inertial compression; fuel magnetization and laser preheat belong only to implementations that specify them.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Target or liner compression must reach sufficient fusion output. MagLIF's pre-magnetization and laser-preheat evidence does not automatically transfer to a different pulsed-power target.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Efficient electrical pulse delivery is potentially useful, but generator energy, energy coupled into fuel, fusion yield and net electricity are distinct boundaries.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Repetition may require replacing targets and parts of the transmission path, clearing debris and recharging. Component-rate demonstrations must match the eventual energy per shot.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: D-T target systems need reproducible fuel loading and a mass balance across target manufacture, burn, debris recovery and breeding infrastructure.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Large transient currents, target debris, mechanical impulse and neutrons stress different components. Consumable hardware and remote replacement need an explicit operating plan.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Modular electrical drivers may offer manufacturing advantages. Those must be weighed against consumables, chamber turnaround, reliable gain and plant integration.

profiles.scope_note: Levitated internal superconducting ring, represented by OpenStar; prototype results and its published D-T plant concept have different evidence status.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: The dipole field supports a distinctive confinement route. Prototype plasma formation and confinement do not establish reactor-density D-T gain or a burning-plasma regime.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Plasma heating, levitation/control, cryogenic management and heat conversion must share one plant ledger; a superconducting ring does not imply negligible operating demand.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Sustained plasma operation must remain compatible with the internal magnet's temperature, energy storage and servicing needs, not just stable magnetic levitation.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: The proposed D-T plant requires breeding, extraction and recycling. Internal structures and access routes must be included when estimating useful blanket coverage.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: An internal cryogenic magnet creates a distinctive shielding and heat-management challenge. Its protection, inspection and replacement must work inside the reactor environment.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: A comparatively simple coil shape may help construction; an internally protected cold component may complicate service. Published plant economics remain design-level estimates.

profiles.scope_note: Electrostatic confinement with magnetic assistance, represented by Avalanche's Orbitron; do not generalize all electrostatic concepts to one electrode geometry.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Maintaining useful ion orbits and reaction rates requires control of particle, collision and electron losses. A voltage milestone does not establish fusion energy gain.

electrical_balance.interpretation: High-voltage input, electron control, cooling and power conversion must be counted against measured fusion output. Compact confinement does not ensure low recirculating demand.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Electrodes, insulators, vacuum quality and particle control must remain stable at the intended operating point. Short tests do not establish useful duty or service intervals.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: Fuel requirements follow the actual reaction, not the device size. D-T testing or operation requires tritium accounting; an advanced-fuel goal needs separate evidence.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Small geometry does not remove neutron, radiation or local heat loads. Electrode protection and replacement need evidence at relevant output and duration.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Small modules could support incremental manufacture. Their economics still depend on actual net output, service life and the repeated balance-of-plant costs around each module.

profiles.scope_note: Xcimer hybrid direct-drive laser target: an initial X-ray stage followed by direct laser drive. This is an inertial approach, not fast ignition or magnetized-target fusion.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: Initial X-ray preparation and later direct drive must produce a sufficiently symmetric, high-gain implosion. Published target calculations do not establish an integrated measured gain.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Hybrid coupling aims to improve energy transfer while retaining useful indirect-drive features. Count every laser pulse, driver inefficiency and plant load in the electrical balance.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Two-sided illumination can simplify chamber openings, but target positioning, repeated high-energy laser operation and chamber recovery must succeed together.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: The D-T capsule and surrounding target require manufacturable fuel loading and recovery. The liquid-salt breeding proposal needs a demonstrated extraction and inventory balance.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: A thick liquid wall is intended to protect permanent structures. Reliable fluid recovery, optical protection, corrosion control and access still require plant-relevant testing.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: The gas-laser, target and liquid-wall combination offers proposed cost advantages. Laser-component progress and accepted design milestones do not validate whole-plant cost or availability.

diagram_sequence: Send two opposed laser beams through openings in a protective cavity.
An initial pulse heats the cavity, producing X-rays that begin capsule ablation and set the initial fuel conditions.
Later pulses illuminate and drive the capsule directly.
The compressed fuel is intended to ignite and burn; show chamber heat capture and reset as proposed plant functions.
profiles.diagram_guardrail: Preserve both coupling stages. Do not show every pulse striking only the hohlraum, every pulse striking only the capsule, a separate fast-ignition heater, or magnetic fuel confinement.

profiles.scope_note: First Light FLARE: electrically driven multi-shell compression followed by separate rapid ignition; inertial family, not a claim of magnetized fuel or classic MagLIF.

plasma_and_fuel_physics.interpretation: A successful compression stage leaves ignition coupling and integrated high gain unresolved. Current compression evidence must not be promoted into a measured ignition result.

electrical_balance.interpretation: Account for both compression and ignition inputs, their electrical efficiencies and all auxiliaries. A modeled target gain requires an explicit combined input boundary.

sustained_operation.interpretation: Fresh engineered targets, compression and ignition timing, chamber reset and both driver systems must operate together repeatedly at relevant energy.

fuel_cycle.interpretation: The D-T multi-shell fuel system needs scalable loading, inventories, unburned-fuel recovery and breeding. Simpler driver requirements do not remove target-factory obligations.

materials_and_maintenance.interpretation: Liners and surrounding structures face debris, transient loads and neutrons. The proposed target architecture needs its own chamber and replacement evidence.

delivery_and_economics.interpretation: Shifting function from the driver into the target can trade machine complexity for manufacturing demands. Partner delivery and integrated cost remain separate from compression validation.

normalization_recommendations.display_label: Laser inertial fusion — hybrid direct drive
diagram_sequence: Send two opposed laser beams through openings in a protective cavity.
An initial pulse heats the cavity, producing X-rays that begin capsule ablation and set the initial fuel conditions.
Later pulses illuminate and drive the capsule directly.
The compressed fuel is intended to ignite and burn; show chamber heat capture and reset as proposed plant functions.
normalization_recommendations.guardrail: Hybrid direct drive is not fast ignition and is not magnetic-inertial confinement. Preserve the initial X-ray stage; do not render Xcimer as ordinary NIF indirect drive or as direct illumination throughout. Research design performance is modeled.
normalization_recommendations.classification_basis: Explicit company and peer-reviewed terminology; current company whitepaper retains the hybrid direct-drive label.

diagram_sequence: Inject and track a fresh target.
Compression lasers illuminate the target from multiple directions.
A separate laser pulse supplies rapid ignition heating.
A proposed blanket and thermal cycle recover fusion energy.
normalization_recommendations.guardrail: Label this as the company's publicly described LIFT reference concept. The separate target-tracking demonstration used surrogate targets; it is not an integrated fast-ignition experiment. Do not assert an unverified final commercial target geometry.
normalization_recommendations.classification_basis: Fast ignition is explicit on the live Japanese company page; direct laser compression follows its described multi-directional target illumination. A separate laser_fast_ignition row is also acceptable if that is the normalized taxonomy.

normalization_recommendations.display_label: Inertial fusion — electrical compression and fast ignition
diagram_sequence: An electrical driver acts on an engineered multi-shell fuel system.
A timed shock sequence assembles dense fuel with limited premature heating.
A separate rapid energy pulse is intended to initiate burn.
normalization_recommendations.guardrail: The reviewed sources do not establish fuel premagnetization or the final ignition-driver implementation. Do not draw MagLIF's axial field and pre-compression laser heating, or the company's historical projectile concept, as the current FLARE architecture. Compression-stage tests did not demonstrate ignition or gain.
normalization_recommendations.classification_basis: Explicit current company description and September 2026 compression-stage test announcement.
